## Erratum — 2026-08-19, Cycle F-1 Task 3

This vector's header claims its "values, exact bytes, length, and identity remain unchanged." That
statement stopped being true the moment Cycle F-1 gave `Geometry` two new fields, `uniforms:
Map<String, ShaderValue>` and `textures: Map<String, ResourceLocator>` (see
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-cycle-f1-stickers-and-geometries-design.md`). This erratum is
appended rather than the header rewritten in place, following the same practice this repository already
uses for a settled decision superseded by later work (e.g. `docs/research/2026-08-18-cycle-c-glb-parse.md`):
rewriting the original text would erase the fact that it was normative under a narrower encoding, at a
time when that narrower encoding was everything Cycle B had built.

**What changed.** `FramePlanCanonicalEncoding.kt`'s `encodeGeometry` gained two appended tagged fields —
field 4 for `uniforms`, field 5 for `textures` — after field 3 (`shaderPair`). Existing tags 1–3 keep
their exact meaning and byte layout; nothing before them in the frame moved. The `RNGC` prefix and schema
byte `01` are unchanged, and the root's `frame`-kind byte (`01`) and `reng-frame-v1` text prefix are
unchanged. Both new fields encode as `CanonicalBinary.list(...)` of tagged `(name, value)` pairs sorted by
key under Kotlin's default `String` ordering (a fixed UTF-16 code-unit comparison, never locale-sensitive)
so that a `Map`'s unspecified iteration order cannot change the digest.

The fixture's `canonicalV1RepresentativeFramePlan()` Kotlin above is **unchanged** — both of its
`Geometry` values still use the original three-argument constructor, so `uniforms` and `textures` both
default to an empty map. The byte growth is therefore exactly two empty-list encodings (a 6-byte field
header plus a 4-byte zero-length count, twice) per geometry, for both geometries in the fixture: 2 ×
2 × 10 = 40 bytes.

**Why extending the encoding was mandatory, not optional.** RenG's frame-to-frame reuse is keyed on plan
content. A `Geometry`'s consumer-supplied uniforms are exactly the mechanism a consumer uses to animate a
custom shader frame to frame (via `uFrameIndex` and any other uniform). If a uniform's value were not part
of the canonical encoding, two plans differing only in that value would produce the *same* frame identity,
and an animating consumer would silently be served a stale frame. That is a correctness bug, not a
completeness gap, so it could not be deferred to a later cycle the way an unrelated field addition might
have been.

**Why this does not need a version bump or a compatibility note for consumers.** Frame identity is
**internal** to RenG — `reng-frame-v1:<lowercase SHA-256>` never appears in `kmp/api/kmp.klib.api`, is not
constructible or readable from outside the library, and no public function returns one. The public
`0.1.0` release (Cycle A) shipped with no public runtime API at all, and Cycle B — the cycle that defined
this vector — has never itself been released; nothing has ever given an external consumer a way to compute
or store a frame identity. There is therefore no external party whose stored digest could disagree with
the one this erratum records. If a later cycle makes frame identity observable through the public API,
that is the point at which changing its encoding would need a version bump and a migration note; until
then, extending it is an internal implementation change like any other.

**The regenerated vector**, produced by the same `canonicalV1RepresentativeFramePlan()` above, run through
the extended encoder:

```text
encoded_bytes=1471
identity=reng-frame-v1:def1b331bc7f074dc94a650083017f171ce9f0f1455d145652ca406b043d81c0
complete_
```

The `minimalFrameHasExactCanonicalLengthAndIdentity` companion vector (not reproduced above; it lives only
in `FramePlanCanonicalEncodingTest.kt`) is unaffected by this change: its plan carries zero geometries, so
the extended `encodeGeometry` never runs and its bytes and identity are exactly as before.
